items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: One day Dickie's parents invited the gang to have supper at their home

ctx.x: There was a bar in Louisville that I had known from the first time I had gone there with Helvey, which was very popular with musicians and entertainers because one could get the best home cooked beans that were ever cooked in this place. For 5 cents you had a big bowl of beans, 5 cents was also the price of a pair of hot dogs and the same price for a big mug of beer. The bread was free and I ate in this place many times even when I had enough money to afford a meal in a good restaurant. I always loved beans and…

One day Dickie's parents invited the gang to have supper at their home They made home brew the same as my father and so many other people did during Prohibition. We were all at the table in the dinning room, eating a fine meal that his mother had prepared when suddenly we heard a noise

as if someone was shooting a pistol in the closet. Then there was the same sound a few seconds later and after that it sounded as if a war had begun. What happened was that Dickie's parents had made a new batch of home made brew and there was a little too much yeast in it. So when the stuff started to formulate, the proportion of yeast made the bottle tops blow off and when someone opened the closed door it was covered with foam. Bottle after bottle blew it's top and there was nothing to do but to let them blow.
